text.p: Koor Industries is not actively negotiating to acquire control of Israel Chemicals Ltd but is interested in principle in acquiring the company, Koor President and CEO Benjamin Gaon said on Monday.

"We are advancing in three areas, one of which is chemicals," Gaon told Reuters. But he added that there had been no negotiations to date with Israel Corp, which holds a controlling 41.9 percent in Israel Chemicals, the largest chemical group in Israel.
Gaon was responding to a newspaper report on Monday that said that Israel Corp was likely to sell its Israel Chemicals holding and that Koor was one of the leading candidates to buy it.
Gaon said that Koor was very much interested in expanding its chemical business, which now consists mainly of the Makhteshim Group. "The subject interests us," he said.

Israel Corp, a holding company, acquired Israel Chemicals from the government of Israel, which remains a minority shareholder. Gaon indicated that the government would have to be consulted on any acquisition.
In addition, the Eisenberg family, which controls Israel Corp, has been in dispute over control of the company since the death of its patriarch Shoul Eisenberg in March.
